impact: No outage: over 90 days the Rootly Agent gave paying teams a final reply without refusing to 90% of their asks, but handed 27.5% of web asks back to the user, against 8.8% in Slack.

scope.users: 3,155 users across 397 paying teams had an agent session in 90 days; 21,403 user messages on chat surfaces
scope.slo: not applicable: product sizing, not an availability or latency SLO

executive_summary: The data pack for the homepage redesign is published as a purple, light and dark artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9347689e-bea8-4593-b86b-a62b70c88d40. Across 21,403 asks from paying teams in 90 days, the agent gave a final reply without refusing to 89.9% (Tier 1, an upper bound because there is no resolution feedback), pointed to docs for 0.78% (Tier 2) and handed back 9.3% (Tier 3). Web, where the homepage will live, hands back 27.5% of asks, mostly because web chat has no incident-update, paging or retro tools. Guardrails and the parity flag were checked and are not material causes. The proposed KR is at least 85% resolved, measured by a real resolution signal; Tier 2 used for config and admin questions; and at most 9% handed back on the homepage (Slack's level), with 5% as a stretch. Braintrust log data and homepage traffic by persona are still missing.
root_cause: Web chat offers most users only read-only tools, so it hands back incident-update, paging and retro asks that Slack completes, and the agent rarely links help-center docs, which leaves Tier 2 almost empty.
trigger: No incident trigger: the homepage redesign kickoff asked for data to size a 3-tier KR before the agent moves from the incident page to a global component.
detection: Measured on request with text rules over ai_session_messages; there is no structured refusal tag or resolution feedback, so no dashboard tracks tier rates today.
resolution: Data pack published; the KR targets and the web write-tool scope are product decisions still to make.
five_whys: More than one in four web asks to the agent ends with the work handed back to the user.
Web chat refuses incident updates, paging and retros that Slack completes.
Web chat keeps only READ_ONLY_TOOLS unless the user passes home-chat gating, and even then it has no incident-update, paging or retro tool.
Write access on web was scoped to the early home-chat rollout and never extended to incident-level actions.
The scope of web write tools for the global agent is a product decision the homepage redesign has to make now.

went_well: Main DB had enough to size every tier, split by surface, cluster intents, check the PRD's prompts and rank manual actions.
Checking the shape of assistant messages caught that 70% are tool-call rows, which corrected Tier 3 from 5.3% to 9.3% before the numbers reached the PRD.
went_wrong: The lane first narrowed to refusals and delivered no artifact, then shipped tier numbers that paired asks with tool-call rows; both needed rework.
Braintrust log reads stayed blocked by the hook, so no trace-level data is in the artifact.
Feedback is empty, so Tier 1 is only an upper bound.
got_lucky: Home chat has almost no volume yet (about 67 sessions), so the web read-only gap has not hit homepage users at scale.
If the 90-day window had covered only Sep 21 to Oct 11, Tier 3 would have read about 4% and the KR target would have been set too low.

summary: Second rework after a rejection with no new guidance. Re-ran the open leads. (1) Method correction: about 70% of assistant rows are JSON tool-call records, so the first pass, which paired each ask with the next assistant row, missed many refusals. Pairing with the turn's last non-JSON reply moves Tier 3 from 5.3% to 9.3% and web from 26.3% to 27.5%, and latency is now time to final reply (8.8s p50). Artifact updated (version 4). (2) h3 invalidated: flipper_gates has 9 actor rows for the parity flag (off for nearly all paying teams), but the flag only gates home/dashboard chat, which has negligible volume; the refusals are on Slack and web. (3) h5 invalidated: 75 off-topic canned replies, 3 on action asks; empty_context 0. (4) The Sep 21 to Oct 5 dip is present on both surfaces after the correction; commit messages don't explain it, so it is a follow-up. (5) Braintrust retried: metadata reads work (projects, monitoring views: none), but log reads stay blocked and the project has no experiments. (6) The funnel was redesigned at the operator's request (labels left, values right, no text cropped). h2 stays the mechanism for web's handback; h6 stays the leading answer. Caveats: keyword intent buckets; refusal rule ~80% precision; manual-action windows mixed and normalized per week.
